agency.name: Zarząd Transportu Miejskiego w Poznaniu
agency.operating_note: This is a rolling short-horizon export, currently about one to two weeks of service per file; routine refreshes are expected.

findings.effort: A column in stops.txt; your scheduling software likely has it.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_boarding to 1 (accessible) or 2 (not accessible) for every stop. A field survey can start with the busiest stops.
findings.what: 3131 of 3131 stops don't say whether a wheelchair user can board there.
findings.why: Riders who use wheelchairs can't plan a trip when accessibility is marked 'unknown'; apps show no information at all.

findings.effort: A default or per-trip field in your export.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_accessible on every trip. If every vehicle is accessible, this may be one default; otherwise use the value for each trip.
findings.what: 36005 of 47868 trips don't say whether the vehicle is wheelchair accessible.
findings.why: Even with accessible stops, riders need to know the transit vehicle itself can take them.

findings.effort: A small file for most flat-fare systems.
findings.fix: Add fare_attributes.txt (or Fares v2 files) with your fare structure. If your service is fare-free, ask to have it marked fare-free instead.
findings.what: The feed contains no fare information.
findings.why: Riders see 'fare unknown' in trip planners and can't budget their trip; visitors are most affected.

findings.what: feed_info.txt has no technical contact (feed_contact_email or feed_contact_url).
findings.why: Trip-planning apps and regional data coordinators have nobody to email when they spot a problem with your feed, so problems linger.

completeness.name: completeness
completeness.summary: 0% of stops state wheelchair accessibility (0% marked accessible, 0% marked not accessible). This measures what the feed publishes, not whether a stop is physically usable. Fare data is not published.

findings.fix: Trim leading and trailing spaces on export. The scorecard's auto-fixed copy already does this.
findings.what: Some values have extra spaces at the start or end.
findings.why: A stray space can break a match, so a stop or route may fail to link across files.

findings.effort: A planned ID change, not a quick text cleanup.
findings.fix: Only change the flagged IDs if an app needs basic ASCII values. Update each place that uses the ID. Keep all names and headsigns in their original language.
findings.what: Some internal IDs use characters outside the basic text set.
findings.why: These IDs are valid UTF-8 data. This warning is only about support in older apps. It does not mean that names in other languages are wrong.

findings.effort: Often a bulk fix in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Use mixed case for stop names and headsigns (e.g. 'Main St & 2nd Ave', not 'MAIN ST & 2ND AVE').
findings.what: Some rider-facing names are in ALL CAPS or all lowercase.
findings.why: ALL-CAPS stop and headsign names are harder to read in apps and are read awkwardly by screen readers.

findings.effort: A few minutes per flagged stop.
findings.fix: Check the flagged stops' coordinates and the route shape in your scheduling software; re-snap whichever is misplaced.
findings.what: Some stops sit far from the route line they belong to.
findings.why: Trip planners may draw the transit vehicle route through the wrong path or point riders to the wrong boarding location.

findings.effort: Usually a re-export from your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Schedule a feed re-export now so the new calendar is live well before the current one ends.
findings.what: This feed's service calendar runs out within the next 30 days.
findings.why: If a new feed isn't published before it ends, trip planners will drop your agency and riders will see no service.

findings.effort: One field, set once in export settings.
findings.fix: Add feed_contact_email or feed_contact_url to feed_info.txt.
findings.what: feed_info.txt lists no contact email and no contact URL.
findings.why: Without a contact, apps like Google Maps can't reach you when they find a problem in the feed.

findings.effort: A field at a time; not urgent.
findings.fix: Review the flagged fields and fill in the ones your riders would use.
findings.what: Some files leave out fields that GTFS asks for but does not require.
findings.why: Recommended fields like agency_phone or stop descriptions make the feed more useful to riders and trip planners.

findings.effort: One setting in most export tools.
findings.fix: Trim past service periods the next time you export.
findings.what: Many of the feed's trips don't run at all in the next 7 days.
findings.why: It usually means old service periods are still in the export, making the feed bigger and harder to check.

findings.effort: Usually a bulk edit in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Set trip_headsign to the trip's last stop or its overall destination.
findings.what: Some trip headsigns name a stop along the way, not the final destination.
findings.why: The sign should tell riders where the transit vehicle ends up, so a midpoint name can send them the wrong way.

findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'future_calendar' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Future calendar (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'future_feed' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Future feed (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: A quick look at the flagged files.
findings.fix: Check the flagged column names for misspellings of standard GTFS fields; remove them if they are vendor extras.
findings.what: Some files contain columns that are not part of the GTFS spec.
findings.why: Harmless to riders, but apps ignore these columns and they can hide typos in real column names.

correctness.name: correctness
correctness.summary: The MobilityData validator flagged 12 kinds of issue across 3979 instances (0 error, 2549 warning, 1430 informational).

findings.fix: Re-export with a validity window that reaches at least 60 days out.
findings.what: Service data runs out in 10 day(s).
findings.why: When the calendar runs out, trip planners stop showing this agency. Fixing it now is calmer than after riders notice.

freshness.name: freshness
freshness.summary: Service data runs out in 10 day(s). Publish an updated feed soon or riders will lose trip planning.

realtime.name: realtime
realtime.summary: Not scored yet. Nothing here counts against the grade.

notes: Realtime quality was not measured this run. It does not count against the grade.
The feed was downloaded from the agency's own URL.

criteria.detail: Service data runs out in 11 days; renew to qualify.
States wheelchair access on 0% of stops and 25% of trips; the mark needs 90% of each.

conformance.summary: This feed is close to the conformance mark. Service data runs out in 11 days; renew to qualify. States wheelchair access on 0% of stops and 25% of trips; the mark needs 90% of each.

feed.license_note: ZTM Poznań's developer terms make the data free to reuse without prior application; name the source, state the last data update, and note that the data was processed.

recommendations.effort: A per-route color setting in your scheduling software.
recommendations.fix: Adjust route_color or route_text_color so each pair clears 4.5:1. Often switching the text between black and white is enough.
recommendations.what: 2 route badge(s) pair a color and text color below the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast bar (6, 13).
recommendations.why: Low-contrast route badges are hard to read for riders with low vision and wash out on a phone screen in sunlight at the stop.

recommendations.effort: A short text field per affected stop; start with the busiest.
recommendations.fix: Add tts_stop_name with the spoken form, e.g. 'Main Street and Second Avenue', for the affected stops.
recommendations.what: 1695 stop name(s) use abbreviations or symbols a screen reader may mispronounce, with no spoken form set ("Głogowska/Hetmańska", "Chludowo/Rynek", "Zielątkowo/Świerkowa", and more).
recommendations.why: Riders who use a screen reader hear the raw name, so 'Main St & 2nd Ave' can come out as 'Main saint' or drop the ampersand.
